newsitem.title: UK: Aerospatiale new head sets recovery as priority.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale new head sets recovery as priority.

text.p: The newly-appointed chairman of Aerospatiale, Yves Michot, said on Sunday his first priority is see through a restructuring plan aimed at returning the group to profit in 1998.
He told reporters ahead of the Farnborough air show, "the top priority is that the restructuring has to be continued so that the financial results will be positive."
The second priority is to define the terms of the planned merger with warplane maker Dassault Aviation by the end of this year as called for by the French government.
He said the Dassault deal would not be a takeover of one company by the other but a real merger with all the activities of each group being brought together into one large entity.

The companies are currently valuing each other's assets and next week are due to exchange information. Aerospatiale is being advised by Lazard, Dassault has retained Paribas while the government has Societe Generale, he said.

A report has to be submitted to the government by the end of December setting out the financial parities for the respective companies, the legal aspects and management structure of the new company, he said.
The merger is expected to lead to pooling the companies' research, purchasing functions, some test flight operations at Istres in southern France and computing systems, he said.
He said the merger should not lead to job losses: 'I do not associate the merger with job losses or site closures.'

The merger would strengthen Aerospatiale's equity base with the entry of Dassault into its capital, he said. This capital opening could lead to a search for other partners, he said. The capital boost should also help the privatisation of Aerospatiale, he added.

partnership into a joint stock company was Michot's third priority, although he said he preferred an evolutionary approach rather than a revolution, retaining as much of the flexibility of the 'groupement d'interet economique (GIE)' partnership as possible.

He envisaged the new Airbus as a prime contractor holding a strong central authority. Due to the needs of national company law in each of the four countries, the new structure would consist of a holding company and subsidiaries in each of the countries.

The 100-seater passenger plane to be built with China and Singapore was a vital issue as it opened up the China market for Aerospatiale's other products such as helicopters and also added to the Airbus family.
Aerospatiale also has to complete mergers of its missiles and satellites activites with Daimler-Benz Aerospace and this should be done as fast as possible, he said.
